clue.text: Capital found on the Thames?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the capital city of Northern Ireland
second meaning: HMS ..., the Second World War cruiser moored as a museum ship on the Thames in London

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second sense: not a city at all but a warship kept on the river in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The same name belongs to Northern Ireland's chief city and to a museum warship permanently berthed in London.

clue.text: Criminal nowhere — Butler did it!

definitions.note: Samuel Butler wrote this satirical novel; the definition is the book he produced

indicators.note: criminal means bent or crooked, so the letters of the next word are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective-story cliche: the crime happened nowhere, and the butler did it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the whodunnit punchline; the butler is the Victorian novelist Samuel Butler, and his imaginary land's name is roughly 'nowhere' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Butler's 1872 satirical novel bears this title, so it is the thing that writer did.

clue.text: Comfortable furniture in airport initially changed

indicators.note: initially changed says the opening letter of the airport's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Luton is an airport north of London

explanation.surface: Cosy seating installed somewhere in an airport has just been replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is an airport north of London; changing its first letter from L to F gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a padded Japanese-style mattress or sofa bed, a piece of soft furniture.

clue.text: Comfortable furniture in place over river

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: to place something is to set it down
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: Cosy seating stands somewhere overlooking a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Settees are upholstered seats for two or more people, a kind of soft furniture.

clue.text: Gentle sound putting butter on bread?

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the butter comes after the bread

parts.note: pita is a flat bread
a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: A soft noise is heard as someone spreads butter on their bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitapat imitates a light, quick tapping, such as raindrops or a heartbeat.

clue.text: See 9
Overwhelming quantity 15, according to the French?

indicators.note: according to the French means spoken in a French accent, which drops the H

parts.note: 15 is the answer to 15-down, 'have lunch'

explanation.surface: A query about whether a huge amount qualifies, as French speakers would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 15-down is HAVE LUNCH; said by a French speaker who drops the H, ''ave lunch' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an avalanche is a huge, overwhelming amount of something arriving at once, like a flood.

clue.text: Speaker's authority in chamber

indicators.note: Speaker's means as said by a speaker, so the word is pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: an oracle is a person or source regarded as an infallible authority

explanation.surface: The Speaker exercises power within the debating chamber of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' and 'chamber' suggest the House of Commons; in fact the chamber is in the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: An auricle is an atrium, one of the upper cavities of the heart, so a chamber of that organ.

clue.text: Drunk low on Stella has Chenin blanc never!

indicators.note: drunk means unsteady and muddled, so the following words are jumbled into new order

parts.words: low on Stella has Chenin blanc

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy on Stella lager refuses outright to drink Chenin blanc wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Stella (Artois) is a lager and Chenin blanc a white wine; all five words from 'low' to 'blanc' are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something with no possibility whatsoever of happening, an emphatic way of saying it won't occur.

clue.text: Forward in Australian city dropping back

indicators.note: dropping back says the final letter of the city's name is lost

parts.note: Perth is the capital of Western Australia

explanation.surface: A forward player in some Australian city team falls back.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of cheeky or impudent; a pert person is boldly saucy.

clue.text: A virtual fool, thirty, dressed up as children's character

indicators.note: dressed up means disguised, so these letters are rearranged
virtual means almost, so the word fool is almost complete, short of its final letter

explanation.surface: A thirty-year-old acting like a fool dons a costume as a figure from children's stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtual' trims fool to FOO; A plus FOO plus THIRTY is then rearranged by 'dressed up'.
explanation.definitionFit: The tooth fairy is the imaginary figure who swaps children's lost milk teeth for coins left under the pillow.

clue.text: See 9
Union in fun dismissing leader

indicators.note: dismissing leader says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: dalliance is light-hearted amorous play, fun

explanation.surface: A trade union having fun gets rid of its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or association formed for mutual benefit, e.g. between nations or parties.

clue.text: Exciting piece from Bremen (thus in German)

indicators.note: piece from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A thrilling excerpt from something written in Bremen, given in German.
explanation.definitionFit: Enthusing means filling with eager enthusiasm, rousing or stirring someone up, so exciting.

clue.text: Eat meat having dropped article inside loin and leg

indicators.note: inside says the trimmed meat goes within the cut of loin and leg

parts.note: a haunch is the leg and loin of an animal as a cut of meat

indicators.note: having dropped says the meat loses the article

parts.note: veal is calf meat
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A butcher's instruction: eat meat, a loin and leg, with an item removed.
explanation.walkthrough: A haunch is a butcher's cut of leg and loin; the article removed is 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lunch is to eat the midday meal, a particular way to eat.

clue.text: Con fixer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a prison officer, slang a ..., who guards convicts
second meaning: a threaded fastener that fixes things together

explanation.walkthrough: 'Con' suggests a swindle or a convict, but here it is defined by what guards convicts in slang; a screw is British slang for a prison warder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both slang for a prison warder and the name of a threaded metal fastener.

clue.text: Prayer about body half lost in heaven?

indicators.note: about means the prayer goes around the other piece

parts.note: an Ave (Ave Maria) is a prayer to the Virgin Mary

indicators.note: half lost means the second half of the word body is gone, leaving its first half

explanation.surface: A prayer for a body that is half lost, wondering if the soul is in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ave Maria is the Catholic 'Hail Mary' prayer; the question mark admits heaven is only one sense of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaven is traditionally imagined as the sky overhead, so being up there is being above.

clue.text: King's predecessor in restaurant listened to old citizen

indicators.note: listened to means we hear the word, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: in the restaurant chain Burger King, the word before King is burger

explanation.surface: In a restaurant someone overheard the predecessor of a king, an old citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's predecessor' suggests royal history; it is the word that precedes King in the fast-food chain's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A burgher was a freeman of a medieval town or borough, a citizen of earlier times.

clue.text: Idiot called when first of messages missed, produced a tweet?

parts.note: a twit is a silly person

indicators.note: missed says that letter is taken out of the word for called

parts.note: termed means called or named

indicators.note: first of means the first letter of messages

explanation.surface: Some idiot rang and, missing the first messages, posted a tweet instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' is past tense, as in named, not phoned.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird twitters when it chirps; the question mark nods at posting on Twitter as well.

clue.text: Tail one wags, extreme part

indicators.note: wags means moves back and forth, so the letters are shaken into new order

explanation.surface: A dog's tail wags at the very end of its body.
explanation.definitionFit: A toenail sits at the tip of a toe, the body's furthest extremity.

clue.text: English poet, sensation

parts.note: Andrew Motion is a British poet, Poet Laureate 1999 to 2009

explanation.surface: An English poet who is a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Motion was the UK's Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is a feeling, and feeling is a common sense of sensation.

clue.text: Attachment to boat behind 25 10 in large ship, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the piece is heard, not spelt, so a word pronounced the same is entered

parts.note: say 25 and 10 (Sioux, pert) and you have the start of supertanker, a large ship; the word that follows them is -anker

explanation.surface: Something fixed to a boat sits behind other items inside a large ship.
explanation.walkthrough: SIOUX (25) plus PERT (10) said together sound like 'super-t', so a supertanker is 'Sioux pert' plus 'anker', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the heavy hooked weight attached to a boat by its cable.

clue.text: Country in Iran having disheartened Slovak, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are mixed up
disheartened means the heart, the two middle letters, is taken from the word Slovak

explanation.surface: A dejected Slovak in Iran has had bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes OV from SLOVAK, leaving SLAK; with IRAN these letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Sri Lanka is an island nation off the southern tip of India, a sovereign state.

clue.text: Off past this London station goes old raconteur in speech?

definitions.text: Off past this London station goes old raconteur in speech?

parts.words: Off past this London station goes old raconteur in speech?
parts.note: the station's name followed by off, said aloud, gives the name of the actor and raconteur Peter Ustinov

explanation.walkthrough: Peter Ustinov was a celebrated actor and raconteur; 'Euston off' said quickly sounds like his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Euston is a London mainline railway terminus, serving trains to the north-west.

clue.text: People in North America (6/4, essentially)

indicators.note: the slash reads as divided by, so one number is split open by the other's core

parts.note: six is the number 6 written out

indicators.note: essentially means only the essence or core of the word four is kept, its outer letters dropped

parts.note: four is the number 4 written out

explanation.surface: A people of North America, described by a cryptic fraction.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the slash as 'divided by': six is split open to take the heart of four.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sioux are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Fur in beard made of ice, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks whether you heard it right, so the answer sounds like the phrase

parts.note: a beard of ice would be a chin chiller, something that makes the chin cold

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a fur coat is in a beard made of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinchilla is the soft grey pelt of a small South American rodent, prized in furriery.

clue.text: God returned in screen idol

indicators.note: returned says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words screen idol, across the gap between them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A deity reappears in the form of a film star.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief deity of Norse mythology, father of Thor.

clue.text: Novelist and ex-con back in custody for sport

parts.note: Jeffrey Archer is a novelist who was jailed for perjury

indicators.note: back in means the last letter of custody

explanation.surface: A novelist and former convict is back in custody, for sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeffrey Archer, best-selling author, served a prison term for perjury in 2001 to 2003.
explanation.definitionFit: Archery is the sport of shooting arrows at a target with a bow.

clue.text: Old lover in affair showing some muscle?

indicators.note: in says the old lover goes inside the affair

parts.note: a fling is a brief romantic affair
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: An old lover reappears in an affair, showing off strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Flexing means tensing or bending, as when displaying biceps to show strength.
